CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md

What this is

zugeo makes GeoArrow a first-class column type in R. It registers every geoarrow.* extension name with zuarrow, keeps geometries in Arrow memory as a geo_vctr, computes bounds, Hilbert keys and spatial sorts over the coordinate buffers, builds flatbush- and kdbush-format packed indexes, and, with qio 0.1.2 in Suggests, reads and writes GeoParquet. Every conversion is exact or an error; a CRS is carried, never resolved or invented. Imports are zuarrow and zujson only, and LinkingTo is zufast (from Stage 3, design D18). No package outside the family appears in DESCRIPTION: sf, wk, geos, s2, geoarrow, nanoarrow, arrow and duckdb are CI-only oracles. No system library. It is not a geometry engine, not a projection library and not an sf replacement; WKB and a CRS string are the bridge to those.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0071. It outranks this file.

Current state

Stage 3 (2026-11-07): conversions between WKB, EWKB, hex WKB, WKT and the native types, coordinates as columns, exact WKT through zufast, and interchange with sf, geos, s2 and wk by WKB. Stage 2 gave geo_vctr over Arrow memory, registered with zuarrow; Stage 1 geo_type_of() and the CRS functions; Stage 0 the package, CI and vendored geoarrow-c. Stage 7 (2026-11-07) added GeoParquet over qio 0.1.2 (R/parquet.R, R/parquet-validate.R). Stage 6 (2026-11-07) added the packed indexes. Stage 4 (2026-11-07) added the lossy policy for edges and the inner-null layout check; Stage 5 (2026-11-07) the kernels, geo_extent, Hilbert keys and geo_validate(). The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is the v0.1.0 issue, created by pkg-roadmap. Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: none yet. qio (GeoParquet), zuclip and zucdt are expected consumers (design §3).

Commands

  • tools/verify-vendor: re-derives src/vendor/ from the pinned commit and fails on any difference. CI runs it (vendor.yaml). Needs cmake, curl, shasum, patch and python3.
  • tools/update-vendor: after changing a pin in tools/derive-vendor, re-derives the tree and rewrites src/vendor/PROVENANCE; then update the commit in src/zgo.h and the versions in test-info.R, inst/COPYRIGHTS and DESCRIPTION.
  • ZUGEO_ORACLES=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "^ci-")': the CI-only oracle tests, with a missing oracle as a failure.
  • Rscript tools/benchmark.R [--n 1000000] [--reps 5]: design §10’s measurements against the installed zugeo, with sf and wk beside it. benchmark.yaml runs it on Ubuntu (the platform §10 names) when the script or workflow changes, or by hand; copy its table into §10.
  • README.Rmd renders with devtools::build_readme(); the article is vignettes/articles/duckdb-to-sf.Rmd (needs duckdb, DBI, sf and qio, which pkgdown.yaml installs).

Architecture

To be written as stages land; see .agents/design.md §4. So far: src/zugeo.c registers the .Call routines (R_forceSymbols, so R calls them by symbol object, .Call(zgo_c_info)); src/zgo.h is the internal header; src/vendor/ is the vendored C, built by the objects listed in src/Makevars (and its copy Makevars.win).

  • src/zgo_schema.c: the schema view, zugeo’s own (design D20), behind geo_type_of(). It reads the ArrowSchema behind any nanoarrow-layout handle (zuarrow’s or nanoarrow’s).
  • src/zgo_build.c: builds schemas from an R spec (zgo_schema(), zgo_spec() in R/build.R), for tests now and export in Stage 2.
  • R/type.R turns the C description into a zugeo_type and parses the extension metadata with zujson; R/crs.R is zugeo_crs, classification and the three equality levels.
  • src/zgo_array.c: is.na(), format() and gathering over a geo_vctr’s chunks; the native walk into geoarrow-c’s GeoArrowVisitor (design D21).
  • R/vctr.R: the geo_vctr class (positions plus chunks, starts, schema attributes) and its methods; R/zzz.R registers the eleven names and the class with zuarrow in .onLoad().
  • src/zgo_convert.c and R/convert.R: every conversion is one walk of the rows (zgo_visit_feature(), shared through src/zgo_array.h) into geoarrow-c’s GeoArrowArrayWriter of the target type; EWKB SRIDs are read before geoarrow-c sees the bytes.
  • src/zgo_index.c and R/index.R: the flatbush R-tree and kdbush k-d tree, built step for step as the JavaScript builds them, with queries and the two-tree join; tools/index-oracle.mjs compares the bytes in node.
  • src/zgo_kernel.c, R/kernel.R and R/extent.R: the per-row kernels as one visitor pass, flatbush’s Hilbert function, validation, and the geo_extent record vector.
  • R/parquet.R and R/parquet-validate.R: GeoParquet over qio (Suggests, called as qio:: behind zgo_need_qio()). zgo_pq_describe() reconciles the geo key with the native GEOMETRY/GEOGRAPHY columns; it is shared by reading, info and validation. No Parquet code in src/.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Nothing outside the family in DESCRIPTION, not even Suggests (design D3). Oracle tests live in tests/testthat/test-ci-*.R, which .Rbuildignore keeps out of the tarball.
  • No JSON code in src/ (D4). Extension metadata, the GeoParquet geo key and PROJJSON go through zujson.
  • The vendored nanoarrow core is namespaced as ZugeoNanoarrow (D2), and every symbol is hidden. An unnamespaced copy clashes with zuarrow’s copy or a loaded nanoarrow.
  • A CRS is never resolved, guessed or dropped (D6). Checks inside zugeo use geo_crs_equal(level = "identical") only (D14).
  • Subsetting and sorting a geo_vctr never copy buffers (D5).
  • Index bytes stay flatbush- and kdbush-compatible (D13).
  • Never edit src/vendor/ by hand. It is tools/derive-vendor’s output, byte for byte; vendor.yaml fails otherwise. A change to vendored code is a patch in tools/patches/, applied in order by the derivation, listed in src/vendor/PROVENANCE (tools/update-vendor writes the list) and marked “Modified for the zugeo R package” in the file it changes. Two so far: 0001 numbers through zufast (D18), 0002 the WKB reader’s bounds (D22).
  • geo_hilbert() must stay bit-identical to flatbush: src/zgo_kernel.c’s zgo_hilbert() is flatbush v4.7.0’s function line for line, and the grid mapping is finish()’s arithmetic in its order. tests/testthat/data/hilbert-flatbush.csv (made by tools/make-hilbert-fixture.js from flatbush’s own source) and DuckDB check it; the index bytes depend on it.
  • Index builds must stay byte-identical to flatbush and kdbush: the sorts in src/zgo_index.c are theirs, pivot and stack order included. A tidier sort changes the bytes. Any offset or item number read from index bytes is checked before use (geo_index_from_raw() takes outside bytes).
  • R CMD check’s registration check needs every .Call() literal: the routine named directly, never through a variable, and no literal NA among the arguments (it crashes the checker); use a named constant such as zgo_no_metadata.
  • R_init_zugeo is the only exported symbol, and no assert, abort or printf is imported. Keep $(C_VISIBILITY), -DNANOARROW_DLL= and src/zugeo-win.def. Don’t rely on -DNDEBUG: the gctorture build ignores it, which is why ryu is not vendored. test-abi.R checks both tables.
  • src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win stay identical.
  • C never raises a zugeo condition. It returns a zgo_failure list (kind, message) and R’s zgo_check() raises it, as zugeo_<kind>_error. Plain Rf_error() is only for misuse of an internal routine. C that holds heap memory must not call R in between (zgo_build.c lets the external pointer own the schema first). zgo_array.c registers every view, writer and built array with a scratch external pointer as soon as it exists; keep that pattern for new C.
  • Unions are built with type ids 0..n-1 and remapped (design D21): nanoarrow builds no other. A new builder over unions must do the same.
  • geoarrow-c’s WKB visit emits its own feat_start() and feat_end(), and a visitor returning EAGAIN (the WKT writer’s size limit) leaves the caller to call feat_end().

Testing

The conformance corpus is geoarrow-data v0.2.0 (design §9), with geoarrow, arrow/pyarrow, DuckDB spatial, sf, geos, s2, wk, gpq, and flatbush/kdbush under node as oracles. The corpus has no union-encoded geoarrow.geometry file; Stage 2 makes one. Helpers: helper-abi.R reads the shared object’s export and import tables (nm, or objdump on Windows; a failure on CI, a skip elsewhere); helper-ci-oracles.R has skip_without_oracle(), which fails under ZUGEO_ORACLES=true (the index oracles also need ZUGEO_NODE_MODULES, a directory with flatbush@4.7.0 and kdbush@4.1.0 installed, and ZUGEO_GEOINDEX_PYTHON, a Python with geoindex-rs); helper-schema.R builds GeoArrow schemas from specs (ga_schema(), ga_union(), ga_field()); helper-corpus.R fetches the corpus; helper-vctr.R reads the union fixture (tests/testthat/data/geometry-union.arrows, zuarrow’s, from tools/make-union-fixture.py) and round-trips data frames. The corpus is never in the package (no licence): it is fetched from geoarrow-data at commit e8eaa04 when ZUGEO_FETCH_FIXTURES=true (set in every CI workflow), or read from ZUGEO_CORPUS_DIR, and checked against tests/testthat/corpus.txt; otherwise the corpus tests skip. helper-convert.R has EWKB builders, bit-for-bit double comparison and the hard doubles of the exactness property test (test-exact.R). The oracle tests compare with sf, geos, s2 and wk by WKB or coordinates, never by WKT text: sf::st_as_text() prints 7 digits, sf::st_as_binary() of a mixed-dimension sfc drops Z, and wk prints the largest double as inf.

Continuous integration

Calls from pedrobtz/r-actions@v1: r-cmd-check.yml (with Windows R-devel added to runners), coverage.yml, the native checks in native-checks.yaml (sanitizers with ASan, valgrind, LTO, rchk, analyzers, cran-special), gctorture.yml (step 1000 on pull requests and pushes under a 10-minute budget, step 20 on a daily schedule), vendor.yml, and vendor-upstream.yml weekly. Its own workflows: pkgdown.yaml, benchmark.yaml, and oracles.yaml, which runs the test-ci-*.R files with ZUGEO_ORACLES=true because r-actions has no workflow for tests outside the tarball, in rocker/r-ver with Posit’s current binaries, with gpq v0.24.0 (ZUGEO_GPQ), then a gdal job in ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal that reads the GeoParquet files the tests leave in ZUGEO_PARQUET_OUT (tools/gdal-oracle.py); fuzz.yaml fuzzes the vendored WKB and WKT readers (tools/fuzz/harness.c, seeds from tools/fuzz/make-corpus.R), short on pull requests and an hour weekly; arch.yaml runs the 32-bit and musl builds weekly. Stages 2, 3 and 6 are full, with the closing three.

Vendored native code

geoarrow-c at commit b3db89f (0.2.0-SNAPSHOT, Apache-2.0), bundled by upstream’s CMake bundler with GEOARROW_NAMESPACE=Zugeo and without fast_float or ryu, and the nanoarrow 0.9.0 release core (not the 0.8.0 geoarrow-c pins, which GCC 16 warns on), bundled by nanoarrow’s own bundle.py and namespaced as ZugeoNanoarrow. No local patches. src/vendor/PROVENANCE has the pins and checksums; inst/COPYRIGHTS the notices.
